notes.statement: In a systematic review of 33 studies covering 107 patients with GACR, most of them case reports, Balfoort et al. (2021) found that protein-restricted diets lowered ornithine levels by 16.0 to 91.2%. Pyridoxine responsiveness was reported for 30% of the included mutations, and lysine supplementation lowered ornithine by 21 to 34%. Other treatments reported were creatine or creatine-precursor supplementation and proline supplementation.
quotes: A total of 33 studies (n = 107 patients) met the inclusion criteria.

Protein-restricted diets lowered ornithine levels ranging from 16.0-91.2%. Pyridoxine responsiveness was reported in 30% of included mutations. Lysine supplementation decreased ornithine levels with 21-34%.
Treatments applied were protein-restricted diets, pyridoxine supplementation, creatine or creatine precursor supplementation, l-lysine supplementation, and proline supplementation.

notes.statement: Balfoort et al. (2021) found no randomized controlled trials or large cohort studies of GACR treatment. They concluded that because no study had predefined clinical outcome measures or structured follow-up, the clinical effectiveness of treatment could not be judged, even though ornithine levels could be lowered.
quotes: No randomised controlled trials or large cohort studies were found.
The lack of pre-defined clinical outcome measures and structural follow-up in all included studies impeded conclusions on clinical effectiveness.

notes.statement: Balfoort et al. (2021) described GACR as a rare inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by biallelic variants in OAT. It is characterized by vision loss beginning early in life that eventually leads to complete blindness, together with high plasma ornithine levels. There is no curative treatment.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GACR) is a rare inborn error of amino acid metabolism caused by bi-allelic variations in OAT. GACR is characterised by vision decline in early life eventually leading to complete blindness, and high plasma ornithine levels.

notes.statement: FRANCOIS et al. (1960) studied carriers ('conductors') of the gene for Fuchs' gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina and discussed it in relation to Alder's anomaly.
quotes: [Conductors of the gene of Fuchs' atrophia gyrata chorioideae et retinae (Alder's anomaly)].

notes.statement: Peltola et al. (2002) found peripheral nervous system involvement in 40 patients with GA: neurographic abnormalities in 21 (53%), which were associated with the severity of ophthalmologic changes and patient age. They concluded that GA is a systemic disease affecting both the CNS and the peripheral nervous system.
quotes: The abnormalities associated with the severity of the ophthalmologic changes and the age of the patients.
These findings of peripheral nervous system involvement in GA suggest that GA is a systemic disease affecting not only CNS but also the peripheral nervous system.

notes.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (2002) followed 2 pairs of sibs with gyrate atrophy on an arginine-restricted diet for 16 to 17 years. In each pair, the younger sib, who began the diet at an earlier age, showed slower progression of chorioretinal lesions than the older sib. The authors concluded that long-term substantial reduction of plasma ornithine levels, if started early, may appreciably slow the progression of the lesions and, to a lesser extent, the progressive loss of retinal function.
quotes: After 16 to 17 years of receiving an arginine-restricted diet, the younger sibling in each pair, who was prescribed the diet at an earlier age than the older sibling, demonstrated a slower progression of lesions compared with the older sibling.

If started at an early age, long-term substantial reduction of plasma ornithine levels may appreciably slow the progression of the chorioretinal lesions and, to a lesser extent, the progressive loss of retinal function in patients with gyrate atrophy.

notes.statement: Caruso et al. (2001) followed 5 patients with gyrate atrophy for 4 to 6 years ahead of a planned gene replacement trial. Median half-lives were 17.0 years for visual field by static perimetry and 11.4 years by kinetic perimetry. Median half-lives for electroretinogram amplitude were 16.0 years for the maximal response and 10.7 years for the flicker response.
quotes: In the 4 to 6 years during which each patient was followed up for this study, median visual field half-lives were 17.0 years (static perimetry) and 11.4 years (kinetic perimetry). Median electroretinogram half-lives were 16.0 years (maximal response) and 10.7 years (flicker response).

notes.statement: Caruso et al. (2001) concluded that visual function often declined slowly in gyrate atrophy. As a result, a long-term clinical trial would be needed to test whether a gene replacement intervention preserves visual function.
quotes: The course of the decline of visual function outcome variables is frequently slow. Thus, a long-term clinical trial would be required to assess the efficacy of the intervention in the preservation of visual function.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2000) put OAT-deficient mice (Oat-/-), made by gene targeting, on an arginine-restricted diet to keep ornithine low over the long term. Over 12 months they followed plasma amino acids, electroretinograms, and retinal histology and ultrastructure. The diet substantially lowered plasma ornithine and completely prevented retinal degeneration.
quotes: we used an arginine-restricted diet to maintain long term reduction of ornithine in a mouse model of OAT-deficiency (Oat(-/-)) produced by gene targeting
We found that an arginine-restricted diet substantially reduces plasma ornithine levels and completely prevents retinal degeneration in Oat(-/-).

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2000) concluded that ornithine accumulation is a necessary factor in the retinal degeneration of gyrate atrophy. They also concluded that restoring OAT activity in the retina is not needed for effective treatment.
quotes: This result indicates that ornithine accumulation is a necessary factor in the pathophysiology of the retinal degeneration in GA and that restoration of OAT activity in retina is not required for effective treatment of GA.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2000) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina as an autosomal recessive disorder caused by ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT) deficiency. It is marked by ornithine accumulation and a progressive chorioretinal degeneration whose cause is unknown.
quotes: Deficiency of ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT) in humans results in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GA), an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by ornithine accumulation and a progressive chorioretinal degeneration of unknown pathogenesis.

notes.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) found by brain MRI degenerative white matter lesions in 50% of patients with gyrate atrophy and premature atrophic changes in 70%, with a striking increase in the number of Virchow spaces; 58% of those with EEG recordings had abnormal slow background activity, focal lesions, or high-amplitude beta rhythm. EEG findings were not associated with MRI changes, age, or sex.
quotes: Brain MRI revealed degenerative lesions in the white matter in 50% of the GA patients, and 70% of the patients had premature atrophic changes, with a striking increase in the number of Virchow's spaces.
The EEG findings were not associated with the MRI changes or with the age or the sex of the patients.

notes.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) found that the brain MRI and EEG findings of 9 gyrate atrophy patients who had received creatine or creatine precursor supplementation daily for several years did not differ from those of 23 untreated patients.
quotes: The MRI or EEG findings of the patients on creatine supplementation did not differ from those of the untreated group.

notes.statement: Valtonen et al. (1999) noted that the retinal and type II muscle fiber findings in gyrate atrophy had been suggested to be mediated by hyperornithinemia-induced deficiency of creatine phosphate, and investigated CNS involvement by analogy with guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency.
quotes: These findings have been suggested to be mediated by hyperornithinaemia-induced deficiency of high-energy creatine phosphate.

notes.statement: Valtonen et al. (1996) found that mean T1 relaxation times of thigh muscle in 7 patients with gyrate atrophy were decreased compared with 6 healthy controls (135 vs 157 ms; p = 0.002), while T2 was slightly but not significantly increased. They concluded that thigh muscles of GA patients universally show changes on CT and MRI, but relaxation time measurements gave little additional information on muscle metabolism.
quotes: Mean T1 relaxation times of the patients were decreased (135 +/- 5 ms) as compared to those of 6 healthy controls (157 +/- 12 ms) (p = 0.002).

Our findings suggest that the thigh muscles of the patients with GA universally show changes in CT and MRI studies, but relaxation time measurements gave little additional information on the muscle metabolism.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1995) used gene targeting to make OAT-deficient mice. Unexpectedly, the newborn mice had low plasma ornithine (hypoornithinemia) and died as neonates. Short-term arginine supplementation rescued them. After weaning, the mice developed hyperornithinemia like that of human gyrate atrophy patients. Over several months they developed a retinal degeneration that involved the photoreceptors and the pigment epithelium. The authors concluded that these mice appeared to be an excellent model of human GA.
quotes: Surprisingly, OAT-deficient mice produced by gene targeting exhibit neonatal hypoornithinaemia and lethality, rescuable by short-term arginine supplementation. Post-weaning, these mice develop hyperornithinaemia similar to human GA patients.
Over several months, OAT-deficient mice develop a retinal degeneration with involvement of photoreceptors and pigment epithelium. OAT-deficient mice appear to be an excellent model of human GA.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1995) concluded that the OAT reaction plays opposite roles in neonatal and adult mammals. This was based on neonatal hypoornithinemia in OAT-deficient mice and transient hypoornithinemia in a human GA infant, followed by hyperornithinemia later in life.
quotes: Thus, the OAT reaction plays opposite roles in neonatal and adult mammals.

notes.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1980) put a patient with gyrate atrophy on an arginine-deficient diet, which lowered her plasma ornithine fivefold over 20 months. About 15 months after starting the diet, her visual function improved, as shown by the electroretinogram, dark adaptation, and color vision. Rod function improved more than cone function. The authors cautioned that the results were preliminary and limited to a single patient, but suggested that a low-arginine diet is beneficial.
quotes: In a patient with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, an arginine-deficient diet has reduced plasma ornithine concentration fivefold during the past 20 months.
The improvement involves rod and, to a lesser extent, cone function.
The results, although preliminary and limited to a single patient, suggest that reduction of plasma ornithine with a low arginine diet is beneficial in this disease.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1980) gave intravenous arginine to 6 patients with gyrate atrophy and 6 controls. Serum arginine curves were similar in the 2 groups. The rise in serum ornithine was more than 3 times greater in patients, and the mean plasma ornithine half-time was 360 min in patients versus 97 min in controls. Patients always excreted less urinary guanidinoacetate than controls, while differences in creatine excretion were less marked.
quotes: The increment in serum ornithine was more than three times as great in patients as in controls. The mean half-times in plasma ornithine were 360 and 97 min, respectively.
The patients always excreted less than the controls, the differences within the sexes being highly significant. Differences in creatine excretion after administration were less marked.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1980) concluded that in gyrate atrophy, high ornithine concentrations inhibit the formation of guanidinoacetate, creatine, and possibly phosphocreatine at the transamidination step (arginine-glycine transamidinase). They suggested that deficiency of high-energy phosphates may underlie the eye and muscle atrophies.
quotes: We conclude that in gyrate atrophy patients, formation of guanidinoacetate, creatine, and possibly phosphocreatine is inhibited at the transaminidation step by the high concentrations of ornithine.
Deficiency of the high-energy phosphates may underlie the pathogenesis of the eye and muscle atrophies.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) found that obligate heterozygotes had a mean serum ornithine slightly higher than normal, with considerable overlap with the normal range, and oral ornithine tolerance tests distinguished carriers from controls in only 1 of 5 cases. Obligate heterozygotes had approximately half-normal OKT activity in fibroblasts.
quotes: Obligate heterozygotes had a mean serum ornithine slightly higher than normal, but there was considerable overlap with the normal range. Oral ornithine tolerance tests distinguished carriers from controls in only one of five cases.
Approximately half-normal levels were found in obligate heterozygotes.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) showed in vitro responsiveness to vitamin B6, with OKT activity in patient fibroblasts increasing at higher concentrations of pyridoxal phosphate.
quotes: In vitro response to B6 was manifest by increased OKT activity at increased concentrations of pyridoxal phosphate in fibroblasts from the patients.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) documented an in vivo response to oral vitamin B6 in 3 of 4 patients, with significant reduction of fasting serum ornithine and increase of lysine.
quotes: In vivo response to vitamin B6 is documented in three of the four patients by significant reduction of fasting serum ornithine and increase of lysine after oral B6 supplementation.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1980) found intracellular inclusions in type 2 muscle fibers on histochemical staining of muscle biopsies; electron microscopy showed tubular aggregates about 60 nm in diameter adjacent to the sarcoplasmic membrane. Oral glucose tolerance testing in 1 patient caused marked changes in serum ornithine and lysine and mild glucose intolerance.
quotes: Histochemical staining of punch muscle biopsies showed intracellular inclusions in type 2 muscle fibers.
Oral glucose tolerance testing in one patient resulted in marked changes in serum ornithine and lysine concentrations, in addition to mild glucose intolerance.

notes.statement: Valle et al. (1980) found that the renal clearances of ornithine, histidine, lysine and the branched-chain amino acids in patients with gyrate atrophy were not high enough to account for the low plasma levels of these amino acids.
quotes: The renal clearances of these four amino acids were not sufficiently elevated to explain their low plasma levels.

notes.statement: Valle et al. (1980) reported that in one patient with gyrate atrophy an arginine-deficient diet progressively lowered plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limit of normal, and ornithinuria and lysinuria disappeared. Oral alpha-aminoisobutyric acid sped up the fall in plasma ornithine by increasing renal ornithine losses.
quotes: In one subject, an arginine-deficient diet led to progressive reduction in plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limits of normal, along with the disappearance of ornithinuria and lysinuria.
Orally administered alpha-aminoisobutyric acid facilitated the fall in plasma ornithine by increasing renal losses of ornithine.

notes.statement: Valle et al. (1980) found that as plasma ornithine approached normal, plasma lysine normalized and plasma arginine became subnormal. Long-term (1.5 year) maintenance on a diet of 10 to 20 g of protein plus essential amino acids kept plasma ornithine between 55 and 355 microM; chorioretinal degeneration did not progress and vision apparently improved.
quotes: When plasma ornithine approached normal (less than 200 microM), plasma lysine became normal, plasma arginine became subnormal, and renal clearances of basic amino acids decreased.

Long-term (1.5 yr) maintenance with a diet containing 10-20 g of protein plus essential amino acids served to keep plasma ornithine at between 55-355 microM; chorioretinal degeneration did not progress and vision apparently improved.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) found trace OAT activity in liver from 2 patients with gyrate atrophy. The mutant enzyme's Km for ornithine was 200 mM, 50 times higher than normal. Raising alpha-oxoglutarate and pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate to 10 times the concentrations that gave maximal activity of the normal enzyme had no effect on the mutant enzyme.
quotes: The Michaelis (Km) value of the mutant enzyme for ornithine was 200 mM, 50-fold higher than normal, but increasing the concentrations of alpha-oxoglutarate and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate to 10 times those giving maximal activity of the normal enzyme had no effect on the mutant enzyme.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) could not show substrate inhibition of the mutant OAT at 1,000 mM ornithine, whereas ornithine above 70 mM inhibited the normal enzyme. They concluded that the mutant enzyme in their 2 patients probably had an altered binding site for ornithine.
quotes: Substrate inhibition of the mutant could not be demonstrated at 1,000 mM ornithine concentration, whereas ornithine concentrations above 70 mM inhibited the normal enzyme.
The data suggest that the abnormal L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase in the two patients studied has an altered binding site for ornithine.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) gave 1.5 g of creatine daily to 7 patients with gyrate atrophy for 1 year. Type II muscle fiber diameters increased from 34.1 to 49.9 micron (P less than 0.001), with no significant change in Type I fibers. Visual fields showed no further constriction, and fundus photography showed slow impairment at an age otherwise associated with rapid progression; the authors called these promising preliminary results.
quotes: we supplemented the diet of seven patients with 1.5 g of creatine daily
There was no significant increase in the diameters of Type I fibers. The visual-field tests showed no further constriction during the therapy.
Fundus photography revealed slow impairment at an age otherwise associated with rapid progression of the disease.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) proposed that part of the disease mechanism may be deficient creatine formation caused by hyperornithinemia, leading to a shortage of cellular phosphocreatine energy stores.
quotes: A pathogenic component of the disease may be deficient formation of creatine, caused by hyperornithinemia, which leads to a shortage of cellular phosphocreatine energy stores.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1981) described gyrate atrophy as marked by progressive constriction of visual fields, a 10- to 20-fold rise in plasma ornithine, and reduced ornithine aminotransferase activity. Atrophy of Type II muscle fibers, morphologically conspicuous but clinically unimportant, progressed along with the eye disease.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is a disease characterized by progressive constriction of visual fields, a 10-fold to 20-fold elevation in plasma ornithine, and depressed activity of L-ornithine:2 oxoacid aminotransferase.
Morphologically conspicuous but clinically unimportant atrophy of Type II muscle fibers progresses concomitantly with the eye disease.

notes.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1983) found that by the second decade, cataract was a uniform finding in patients with gyrate atrophy. The opacities lay mainly along the confluence of the posterior sutures, in the visual axis, and appeared to be unique compared with cataracts associated with other forms of retinal degeneration.
quotes: By the second decade, cataract is a uniform finding in patients with gyrate atrophy and appears to be unique as compared with cataracts associated with other forms of retinal degeneration.

notes.statement: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1983) examined 3 cataractous lenses removed from gyrate atrophy patients aged 31 to 47 years. Under the microscope, the posterior suture region was filled with liquified, degenerated lens material typical of senile cataractous changes.
quotes: The gross and microscopic examination of three cataractous lenses removed from patients 31 years to 47 years of age is reported.
Histologically the region of the posterior sutures was filled with liquified and degenerated lens material typical of senile cataractous changes.

notes.statement: Fukuda et al. (1983) found that in 2 brothers with gyrate atrophy and hyperornithinemia, ornithine concentrations were elevated in erythrocytes, lymphocytes, and granulocytes to differing degrees depending on cell type, and aspartic acid concentrations were low in erythrocytes.
quotes: We found that ornithine concentrations were elevated in blood cells, to different degrees depending on the type of cell, and that aspartic acid concentrations were low in erythrocytes.

notes.statement: Fukuda et al. (1983) found that after oral ornithine administration, blood cell ornithine concentrations in the patients peaked at 2 hours and remained high for at least 4 hours, with concentration curves differing among the 3 cell types after 2 hours.
quotes: The ornithine concentration in the blood cells of the patients reached a peak 2 h after the oral administration, and remained high for at least 4 h, although after 2 h the concentration curves differed in the three types of cells.

notes.statement: McInnes et al. (1981) treated a 15-year-old patient with hyperornithinemia and gyrate atrophy with a low-arginine diet that lowered plasma ornithine to near normal (0.15-0.25 mmol/l). After 5 weeks, visual function improved in one eye that had been severely impaired, with no improvement, for 3 years. The improvement lasted until diet compliance worsened at 8 months, after which vision regressed toward pretreatment status.
quotes: was given a low-arginine diet to reduce plasma ornithine to a concentration (0.15--0.25 mmol/l) near the normal range
After five weeks of treatment, there was improvement in the visual function of one eye which had been severely impaired without improvement for 3 years.
This improved visual function was maintained until compliance with the diet deteriorated at eight months, after which visual function regressed towards pretreatment status.

notes.statement: McInnes et al. (1981) found that overrestriction of dietary arginine caused hyperammonemia. They concluded that arginine is an essential amino acid in ornithine transaminase deficiency.
quotes: Overrestriction of dietary arginine produced hyperammonaemia, indicating that arginine is an essential aminoacid in ornithine transaminase deficiency.

notes.statement: McInnes et al. (1981) suggested that lowering plasma ornithine may reverse a metabolic neuroretinopathy in gyrate atrophy. They also suggested it might halt progression of the retinal atrophy.
quotes: These results suggest that reduction of plasma ornithine may reverse a metabolic neuroretinopathy in this disease, and offer hope that progression of the retinal atrophy can be arrested as well.

notes.statement: François et al. (1966) wrote about gene carriers of Fuchs gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (atrophia gyrata choroideae et retinae).
quotes: [Apropos of gene carriers of Fuch's atrophia gyrata choroideae et retinae].

notes.statement: Simell and Takki (1973) reported raised plasma ornithine in association with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: Raised plasma-ornithine and gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.

notes.statement: Wirtz et al. (1985) found that fibroblasts from 4 pyridoxine-responsive gyrate atrophy patients had higher ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity in cell homogenates and greater incorporation of radioactivity from 14C-ornithine into protein in intact cells than fibroblasts from 3 non-responsive patients.
quotes: Responsive patients had higher activity of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) in cell homogenates and greater incorporation of radioactivity from 14C-ornithine into protein in cultured cells in situ compared to non-responsive patients.

notes.statement: Wirtz et al. (1985) did complementation analysis on fused fibroblasts from 7 patients, using the ratio of 14C-ornithine to 3H-leucine incorporation into protein. They found no positive complementation, which suggested that pyridoxine-responsive and non-responsive gyrate atrophy are caused by different allelic mutations at the same OKT locus.
quotes: Complementation analysis of the cells from these seven patients was performed, based on the ratio of incorporation of 14C/3H into protein in fused cells incubated in 14C-ornithine and 3H-leucine.

Lack of positive complementation in these crosses suggests that pyridoxine responsive and non-responsive patients with gyrate atrophy represent different allelic mutations of the same genetic locus coding for OKT.

notes.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) used a cDNA clone encoding human ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) to map OAT gene sequences to chromosome regions 10q26 and Xp11.2, using somatic cell hybrids and in situ hybridization.
quotes: By means of a complementary DNA clone encoding human OAT, the OAT gene sequences were mapped by somatic cell hybrids and in situ hybridization to human chromosome regions 10q26 and Xp11.2.

notes.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) reviewed 80 biochemically confirmed cases of gyrate atrophy. The review confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance and supported the presence of a functional OAT gene on chromosome 10.
quotes: A review of 80 biochemically confirmed cases of gyrate atrophy confirmed the autosomal recessive inheritance of this disease and supported the presence of a functional OAT gene on chromosome 10.

notes.statement: Barrett et al. (1987) noted that the X-chromosome OAT gene sequences (Xp11.2) mapped to the same region as L1.28 (Xp11.0-p11.3), a marker closely linked to X-linked recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
quotes: Interestingly, the X chromosome OAT gene sequences (Xp11.2) map to the same region as L1.28 (Xp11.0-p11.3), a marker closely linked to X-linked recessive retinitis pigmentosa.

notes.statement: Mitchell et al. (1988) found that if translation started at the nearest in-frame methionine codon, the initiator codon mutation would shorten OAT by 138 amino acids. This would remove the whole mitochondrial leader sequence and 113 amino acids of the mature peptide.
quotes: Initiation of translation at the closest in-frame methionine codon would truncate OAT by 138 amino acids, eliminating the entire mitochondrial leader sequence and 113 amino acids of the mature peptide.

notes.statement: Mitchell et al. (1988) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina as an autosomal recessive chorioretinal degeneration. It is caused by deficiency of ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT), an enzyme of the mitochondrial matrix.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GA) is an autosomal recessive chorioretinal degeneration caused by deficiency of the mitochondrial matrix enzyme, ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT).

notes.statement: Mitchell et al. (1988) cloned and sequenced the human OAT cDNA and worked out the intron-exon structure of the gene. RNase A protection showed a probe-target mismatch at the 5-prime end of the first coding exon in the patients.
quotes: we cloned and sequenced the human OAT cDNA and determined the intron-exon arrangement of the structural gene
We found a probe-target mismatch at the 5' end of the first coding exon

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1988) found that fibroblasts from heterozygotes for both the pyridoxine-responsive and the pyridoxine-nonresponsive variants of gyrate atrophy had intermediate levels of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity.
quotes: Fibroblasts from heterozygotes for the pyridoxine-responsive variant as well as those for the pyridoxine-nonresponsive variant contain intermediate levels of OKT activity.

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1988) distinguished carriers of the two variants by how much OKT activity rose with pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) in vitro. The ratio of activity at 0.04 mM PLP to activity at 0 mM PLP was 1.18 +/- 0.18 in controls (N = 12), 1.43 +/- 0.26 in pyridoxine-nonresponsive heterozygotes (N = 5), and 2.20 +/- 0.14 in pyridoxine-responsive heterozygotes (N = 3).
quotes: These two variants can be distinguished by the in vitro responsiveness of OKT activity to pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) stimulation.

The ratios of OKT activity at 0.04 mM PLP compared with activity at 0 mM PLP were, respectively, lowest for controls (1.18 +/- 0.18; N = 12), intermediate for pyridoxine-nonresponsive heterozygotes (1.43 +/- 0.26; N = 5), and highest for pyridoxine-responsive heterozygotes (2.20 +/- 0.14; N = 3).

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1988) stated that gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina caused by OKT deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina that is due to ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) studied OAT in fibroblast mitochondria from 9 patients with gyrate atrophy. The apparent Km for pyridoxal phosphate was higher in the 4 pyridoxine-responsive patients than in nonresponsive patients, whose Km for PLP was normal. The apparent Km for ornithine was normal in all 7 patients studied.
quotes: The apparent Km for PLP was higher in pyridoxine-responsive patients than in nonresponsive patients whose apparent Km for PLP was normal.
In contrast, the apparent Km for ornithine was normal in the seven patients studied.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) found that the pyridoxine-responsive patient with the mildest clinical disease had the highest Km for PLP. However, she had the most stable enzyme, which they suggested presumably contributed to her milder phenotype.
quotes: Surprisingly, the responsive patient with mildest clinical disease had the highest Km for PLP. However, she had the most stable enzyme, which presumably contributed to her milder phenotype.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1989) concluded from Western blot and kinetic data that gyrate atrophy is heterogeneous both within and between the pyridoxine-responsive and nonresponsive groups. OAT protein was clearly detectable in responsive patients and in 2 of 5 nonresponders, but was low or undetectable in the other 3 nonresponders.
quotes: Western blot analyses of mitochondrial proteins, using antibody to human OAT, indicated clearly detectable OAT protein in pyridoxine-responsive patients and in two of five nonresponders, but low or undetectable levels in the other three patients.
These data clarify the mechanism of pyridoxine response and indicate heterogeneity within as well as between the pyridoxine-responsive and the nonresponsive patients with gyrate atrophy.

notes.statement: Ramesh et al. (1988) defined 6 RFLPs at the OAT locus, all mapping to chromosome 10, with an overall heterozygosity of 83%. In the one available pedigree, the OAT locus segregated concordantly with gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The RFLPs, which are detected by noncoding single-copy probes from the OAT gene and by subclones of the HOAT1 cDNA, all map on human chromosome 10, producing an overall level of heterozygosity for the OAT locus of 83%.
Using the RFLPs, we have determined that the OAT locus segregates concordantly with GA in one available pedigree.

notes.statement: Ramesh et al. (1988) found significant linkage disequilibrium between OAT RFLPs and gyrate atrophy. They considered this genetic evidence that a defect in the OAT structural gene causes the disorder.
quotes: Furthermore, the RFLPs display significant disequilibrium with GA, providing genetic evidence implicating a defect in the OAT structural gene as the cause of this disorder.

notes.statement: Ramesh et al. (1988) suggested that OAT RFLPs could potentially be used for prenatal diagnosis and carrier detection in families with a previous history of gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The RFLPs for OAT are potentially applicable to prenatal diagnosis and carrier detection in families with a previous history of GA.

notes.statement: Brody et al. (1992) identified 21 new OAT alleles in patients with gyrate atrophy. They studied these and 3 previously described mutations in cultured fibroblasts. Most alleles (20 of 24) produced normal amounts of normally sized OAT mRNA, but only 2 of 24 produced normal amounts of OAT antigen.
quotes: we discovered and molecularly characterized 21 newly recognized ornithine delta-aminotransferase alleles

The majority (20/24) of these alleles produce normal amounts of normally sized ornithine delta-aminotransferase mRNA. By contrast, only 2/24 had normal amounts of ornithine delta-aminotransferase antigen.

notes.statement: Brody et al. (1992) recreated the mutations by site-directed mutagenesis and expressed the mutant OAT in Chinese hamster ovary cells. These experiments confirmed that several of the mutations inactivate OAT and cause gyrate atrophy in the patients.
quotes: Reproducing these mutations by site-directed mutagenesis and expressing the mutant ornithine delta-aminotransferase in Chinese hamster ovary cells confirms that several of these mutations inactivate ornithine delta-aminotransferase and cause gyrate atrophy in these patients.

notes.statement: Kennaway et al. (1977) found deficient activity of ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase in cultured skin fibroblasts from patients with gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina: deficient activity of ornithine ketoacid aminotransferase in cultured skin fibroblasts.

notes.statement: Stoppoloni et al. (1978) found that restricting protein intake to a minimum of 0.8 g/kg/day significantly lowered plasma ornithine levels in a 3-year-old girl with gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The restriction of protein intake to a minimum of 0.8 g/kg/day induced a significant reduction of plasma ornithine levels.

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1978) found that cultured skin fibroblasts from 5 patients with gyrate atrophy had virtually no ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) activity. Fibroblasts from 4 carrier parents had 42 to 65% less OKT activity than normal.
quotes: Cultured skin fibroblasts from five affected patients showed a virtual absence of ornithine ketoacid transaminase (OKT) (L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase E.C.2.6.1.13) activity.
Fibroblasts from four carrier parents showed a 42%-65% reduction in OKT activity.

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1978) found that raising the pyridoxal phosphate concentration in the assay partly restored OKT activity in fibroblasts from 1 of 5 patients. They concluded that gyrate atrophy is genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: Increasing the concentration of pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6 in the assay media resulted in partial restoration of OKT activity in fibroblasts from one out of five patients studied.
genetic heterogeneity exists in this disease

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1978) described gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina as a chorioretinal degeneration associated with hyperornithinemia, inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is a chorioretinal degeneration associated with hyperornithinemia with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.

notes.statement: Shih et al. (1978) concluded that OKT deficiency is closely associated with the genetic defect in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina.
quotes: We conclude that OKT deficiency is closely associated with the genetic defect in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina

notes.statement: O'Donnell et al. (1978) found that cultured fibroblasts from a patient with gyrate atrophy of the retina did not convert uniformly 14C-labeled L-ornithine to proline, a metabolic block caused by deficient L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase activity. The patient's heterozygous father had intermediate enzyme activity.
quotes: Cultured fibroblasts from a patient with gyrate atrophy of the retina do not convert L-ornithine, uniformly labeled with carbon-14, to proline.
This metabolic block is caused by deficient L-ornithine:2-oxoacid aminotransferase activity in the patient. Her heterozygote father has intermediate activity of this enzyme.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1979) found that in gyrate atrophy the number of type 2 muscle fibers decreased with age, and that females as well as males had tubular aggregates, the sexes being affected equally; gyrate atrophy was the first disease in which females were shown to have tubular aggregates.
quotes: Gyrate atrophy is the first disease in which females are shown to have tubular aggregates; the sexes were affected equally.
In gyrate atrophy the number of type 2 fibers decreases with age.

notes.statement: Sipilä et al. (1979) suggested that the muscle and eye changes in gyrate atrophy are probably related to abnormal creatine synthesis caused by the increased body pool of ornithine, and that muscle abnormalities may also be present in other tapetoretinal dystrophies.
quotes: The muscle and eye changes are probably related to abnormal creatine synthesis, caused, in gyrate atrophy, by the increased body pool of ornithine; muscle abnormalities may also be present in other tapetoretinal dystrophies.

notes.statement: Valle et al. (1977) found no detectable ornithine aminotransferase activity in phytohemagglutinin-stimulated lymphocytes from a patient with gyrate atrophy. In cells from her heterozygous daughter, activity was 44% of normal values. [3H]thymidine incorporation and other transformation-affected enzymes confirmed that the patient's cells were transformed, which showed an enzyme deficiency in gyrate atrophy.
quotes: The patient's cells had no detectable ornithine aminotransferase activity, and the activity in the heterozygote's cells was 44% of normal values.

Measurements of [3H]thymidine incorporation and other transformation-affected enzymes verified that the patient's cells were transformed. These results demonstrate an enzyme deficiency in gyrate atrophy.
